newsitem.title: GERMANY: German Bunds, Bobls end volatile trade higher.
newsitem.headline: German Bunds, Bobls end volatile trade higher.

text.p: German Bunds and Bobl future ended a volatile session on Thursday in positive territory after the impact of leaked reports showing high unemployment levels underpinned trading sentiment over the day.
Bunds were able to stave off some pressure from profit-taking to end the day higher.
"The market trading sideways in the United States meant took the wind out of the sails of the German debt market as well," said one trader.
The market was now looking ahead to final details of U.S. unemployment data for May, due at 1230 GMT on Friday.
The market would also be looking out for German jobless data for May, which would be released officially at around 0755 GMT.
The July 2007 Bund ended at 101.29 points, with yield at 5.82 percent, while the September after closing on Wednesday at 101.21 points.
The September Bund future ended at 100.50, up from its closing price on Wednesday of 100.40 points, having traded in a range between 100.27 points and 100.68 points over the day.
